comments.body: The interesting common thread is that both techniques make complexity readable by choosing what not to preserve. Skeleton-Guided Edge Bundling gives up exact individual edge tracing to reveal corridors, while Image-Based Crowd Rendering gives up full per-person geometry to make a populated city feel visually present.

sections.body: Across the edge-bundling and crowd-rendering sources, dense visual scenes become manageable by replacing raw geometric complexity with structured image-space or sample-based abstractions. Skeleton-based edge bundling clusters geometrically similar edges, inflates cluster shapes, extracts skeletons, and attracts edges toward locally centered targets; image-based crowd rendering uses impostor samples, positional and directional discretization, and optimized texture storage to display large animated crowds at interactive rates.
sections.heading: Shared abstraction strategy

sections.body: The shared concept is not merely acceleration: abstraction changes what the viewer can read. Edge bundling sacrifices individual edge identity and direction fidelity to expose coarse connectivity, while crowd impostors trade full per-avatar geometry for scalable visual presence. Shader raymarching provides a related but weaker bridge because it also treats geometry through mathematical spatial descriptions, marching rays through distance fields inside a fragment shader.
sections.heading: Readable but partial representations

title: Image-space geometric abstraction for readable visual complexity
